entries.name: docsify
entries.use_for: Turn Markdown files into a docs site at runtime with no build step.
entries.why: Zero-build setup: drop an index.html next to your Markdown; ideal for small projects.
entries.summary: Documentation site generator that renders Markdown files into a website at runtime, with no build step and no statically built HTML. It includes a full-text search plugin, multiple themes, emoji support and a plugin API, and can be served from any static server or GitHub Pages.
entries.best_for: Quickly publishing lightweight docs from Markdown on GitHub Pages or a static host without any build pipeline.
entries.not_for: Sites that need prebuilt static HTML for SEO or no-JavaScript readers, since pages are rendered in the browser rather than generated at build time.

entries.name: Docus
entries.use_for: Write documentation sites with Nuxt and Markdown.
entries.why: Nuxt-based docs theme from the Nuxt Content team; good fit for Vue/Nuxt projects.
entries.summary: Docs framework and CLI (npx create-docus) that scaffolds a documentation site built on Nuxt 4, Nuxt UI and Tailwind CSS, written in Markdown with Vue/MDC components. It includes dark mode, i18n, search, SEO helpers, llms.txt generation, a built-in MCP server at /mcp, Agent Skills publishing and an optional AI assistant powered by Vercel AI Gateway.
entries.best_for: Teams in the Vue/Nuxt ecosystem wanting a modern docs site with built-in AI features (MCP server, llms.txt, chat assistant).
entries.not_for: React-based teams or anyone avoiding Nuxt/Vue. The AI assistant depends on Vercel AI Gateway, so that part requires an external service.

entries.name: Docusaurus
entries.use_for: Build documentation websites with versioning, i18n and search from Markdown/MDX.
entries.why: Most widely used docs framework, maintained by Meta; strong plugin ecosystem.
entries.summary: Tool for building, deploying and maintaining open source project websites, handling the site build so authors focus on content. It ships a home page, docs section, blog and support pages out of the box, is customizable, and supports localization via Crowdin.
entries.best_for: Open source projects and teams wanting a documentation site with a docs section, a blog and translation support.
entries.not_for: Minimal single-page docs where a full site generator is overkill, or teams avoiding a React/Node-based toolchain.

entries.name: Doxygen
entries.use_for: Generate API docs from annotated C, C++ and other sources
entries.why: The standard documentation generator for C/C++
entries.summary: Generates documentation from annotated source code, primarily C++ but also C, Objective-C, C#, PHP, Java, Python, Fortran, VHDL and others. It outputs HTML and LaTeX, plus RTF, PDF, DocBook and man pages, can extract structure from undocumented code, and draws include, inheritance and collaboration graphs.
entries.best_for: API reference documentation for C/C++ and other compiled-language codebases, or exploring the structure of large unfamiliar source trees.
entries.not_for: Modern Markdown-first docs websites or guides; it is focused on reference docs extracted from source comments.

entries.name: Fumadocs
entries.use_for: Build documentation sites in Next.js (and other React frameworks) with MDX.
entries.why: Flexible docs framework that lives inside your app; popular in the Next.js ecosystem.
entries.summary: Framework for building documentation websites inside React frameworks and Astro. It officially supports Next.js, Astro with React, and Vite-based Tanstack Start, Waku and React Router; all packages are ESM only.
entries.best_for: Adding a documentation site to an existing Next.js or other React-framework app, or building docs within Astro using React.
entries.not_for: Projects that cannot use ESM-only packages, or non-React stacks such as Vue. The README is brief; feature details are on its documentation site.

entries.name: JSDoc
entries.use_for: Generate API documentation sites from JavaScript comments
entries.why: The original JS API doc generator; JSDoc comment syntax is also what TypeScript and editors understand.
entries.summary: API documentation generator for JavaScript that builds docs from JSDoc comments in source code. A community ecosystem adds templates (e.g. better-docs), Grunt/Gulp plugins, a GitHub Action, and jsdoc-to-markdown for Markdown output.
entries.best_for: Generating HTML API reference docs for JavaScript libraries from JSDoc comments.
entries.not_for: Narrative documentation sites or guides; it generates API reference only. TypeScript projects may prefer TypeScript-native doc generators.

entries.name: Jupyter Book
entries.use_for: Build publication-quality books and docs from Markdown and Jupyter notebooks.
entries.why: Best option when docs include executable notebooks or scientific content.
entries.summary: Open-source tool for building publication-quality books and documents from Markdown files or Jupyter notebooks containing code cells. A single command executes the code, caches outputs, and produces a web-based interactive book and a PDF, with citations, cross-references and numbered equations.
entries.best_for: Scientific, educational or data-analysis content that mixes prose with executable code and needs both a web book and a PDF.
entries.not_for: Plain product docs without computational content. The current version differs from the Sphinx-based v1, which now lives in the v1 branch.

entries.name: Material for MkDocs
entries.use_for: Feature-rich MkDocs theme and docs framework with search, versioning and blog
entries.why: The most popular docs framework in the Python world (used by FastAPI, Pydantic and many more)
entries.summary: Theme and documentation framework on top of MkDocs that turns Markdown into a professional static site. Installed with pip and enabled in mkdocs.yml, it provides search, responsive layouts, support for over 60 languages, and configuration of colors, fonts, icons and logo. MIT licensed.
entries.best_for: Teams wanting a polished, searchable static docs site from Markdown with minimal configuration and self-hosted output.
entries.not_for: Docs needing React/Vue components embedded in pages; it requires the Python-based MkDocs toolchain.

entries.name: mdBook
entries.use_for: Create online books and docs from Markdown
entries.why: Official Rust tool behind The Rust Book; fast single binary
entries.summary: Command-line utility from the Rust project that creates online books from Markdown files. Its User Guide documents features, installation and usage, and is itself an example of a generated book.
entries.best_for: Book-style technical documentation or tutorials written in Markdown, especially in Rust projects, deployed as a static site.
entries.not_for: Docs sites needing blogs, landing pages or component-rich layouts; it is focused on book-style output. The README is minimal, so check the User Guide for features.

entries.name: mkdocstrings
entries.use_for: Auto-generate API reference pages in MkDocs from docstrings
entries.why: Standard API-docs plugin for MkDocs
entries.summary: MkDocs plugin that generates documentation automatically from source code. It is language-agnostic through handlers (including Python and shell scripts), supports multiple themes per handler, and enables cross-references between pages and across sites similar to Sphinx's intersphinx.
entries.best_for: Adding auto-generated API reference pages to an MkDocs (often Material for MkDocs) site, especially for Python libraries.
entries.not_for: Projects not using MkDocs, or languages without an available handler. It produces API reference inside MkDocs, not a standalone site.

entries.name: Nextra
entries.use_for: Next.js-based docs and blog framework with MDX
entries.why: Popular Next.js docs framework from the Vercel ecosystem
entries.summary: Site generation framework built on Next.js, distributed as the nextra package with a nextra-theme-docs theme for documentation sites. The README is brief and points to nextra.site for documentation.
entries.best_for: Building a documentation site with Next.js using the nextra-theme-docs theme.
entries.not_for: Teams not using Next.js or React. The repository README gives little feature detail; check nextra.site before relying on specific capabilities.

entries.name: pdoc
entries.use_for: Auto-generate API documentation for Python projects from docstrings and type hints.
entries.why: Zero-config and simple; good for library API references.
entries.summary: Generates API documentation for Python projects from modules and docstrings, focused on simplicity. It supports type annotations, numpydoc and Google-style docstrings, auto-links identifiers, respects __all__, has a built-in live-reloading web server and outputs standalone HTML with customizable templates.
entries.best_for: Quickly producing clean API reference docs for a Python package with a single command and no configuration.
entries.not_for: Complex documentation needs; the README recommends Sphinx for those. Not affiliated with the separate pdoc3 project.

entries.name: Redoc
entries.use_for: Render OpenAPI/Swagger specs as a three-panel API reference site.
entries.why: Battle-tested OpenAPI renderer with a CLI for static bundles.
entries.summary: Open source tool that generates API reference documentation from OpenAPI (3.2/3.1/3.0, Swagger 2.0), AsyncAPI 3.x and GraphQL SDL definitions in a responsive three-panel layout with search, navigation and request/response examples. It is available as an HTML tag, React component, Redocly CLI and Docker image, with theming, dark mode and code samples.
entries.best_for: Publishing read-only API reference docs from an OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL spec, embedded in an existing site or built as static HTML.
entries.not_for: Try-it consoles, mock servers, automated code samples, lint or SOAP; the README lists these under Redocly's hosted offering, not the community edition.

entries.name: Rspress
entries.use_for: Fast static docs site generator built on Rsbuild/Rspack
entries.why: ByteDance's Rust-powered docs SSG with quick builds at scale
entries.summary: Static site generator built on Rsbuild and an MDX compiler, aimed at documentation. It lets you use React components in Markdown via MDX, builds a full-text search index automatically, outputs static HTML, supports component demo previews, and has a plugin system for customizing build and theme.
entries.best_for: React/MDX-based documentation sites, including component library docs, that want fast builds and built-in search.
entries.not_for: Non-React stacks. It is tied to the Rsbuild/Rstack toolchain.

entries.name: Scalar
entries.use_for: Interactive OpenAPI API reference with built-in API client, embeddable in many frameworks.
entries.why: Modern alternative to Swagger UI with integrations for Express, FastAPI, Next.js and more.
entries.summary: Renders OpenAPI/Swagger documents as an interactive API reference with a built-in API testing tool and generated code examples for many languages. Also ships an offline-first, open-source API client for OpenAPI. Can be dropped into a single HTML file from a CDN or added through framework integrations such as ASP.NET Core.
entries.best_for: Publishing interactive API reference docs from an existing OpenAPI/Swagger spec, or testing APIs with an OpenAPI-aware desktop/browser client.
entries.not_for: Needs an OpenAPI/Swagger document; not a general prose documentation site generator. Managed hosting with custom domains and team features is a hosted service, partly paid.

entries.name: Sphinx
entries.use_for: Generate documentation sites, PDFs and API references for Python projects.
entries.why: The standard Python documentation tool behind Read the Docs and most Python libraries.
entries.summary: Python documentation generator that uses reStructuredText and Docutils to build documentation. Outputs HTML, PDF, plain text, EPUB, TeX, man pages and more, with cross-references, automatic indices, a document tree, Pygments code highlighting and Jinja2 templating.
entries.best_for: Technical and API documentation for Python projects or any project needing multi-format output (HTML, PDF, EPUB) with rich cross-referencing.
entries.not_for: Built around reStructuredText rather than plain Markdown; not a JavaScript/React-style modern docs site framework or an interactive API reference renderer.

entries.name: Starlight
entries.use_for: Build documentation sites with Astro, including search, i18n and navigation out of the box.
entries.why: Astro's official docs theme; fast static output, accessible defaults, any UI framework.
entries.summary: Starlight is a documentation website framework built for Astro. Its own documentation site is built with Starlight.
entries.best_for: Building a documentation website when you are using or willing to use Astro.
entries.not_for: Tied to the Astro framework; it is a docs site framework, not an API reference generator or general app framework.

entries.name: Swagger UI
entries.use_for: Render interactive API docs from an OpenAPI spec
entries.why: The most widely deployed OpenAPI doc renderer
entries.summary: Generates interactive visual documentation from an OpenAPI (formerly Swagger) specification so users can explore and call API resources without implementation logic. Published as npm modules: swagger-ui for bundled single-page apps and swagger-ui-dist, a dependency-free build for serving from server-side projects.
entries.best_for: Embedding or serving interactive API docs directly from an OpenAPI/Swagger spec in a web app or backend.
entries.not_for: Requires an OpenAPI spec; not a general docs site. README lists known 3.x gaps such as no JSON Form Editor, partial collectionFormat support and no l10n.

entries.name: TypeDoc
entries.use_for: Generate API reference docs from TypeScript sources
entries.why: Standard API doc generator for TypeScript
entries.summary: Documentation generator for TypeScript projects. It reads tsconfig.json and package.json to find entry points and compiler options, then writes HTML docs (or JSON) via a CLI or config file, with themes and a packages mode for monorepos.
entries.best_for: Generating API reference docs from TypeScript source code, including merged docs for monorepo packages.
entries.not_for: Only for TypeScript projects; produces API reference from code, not a hand-written docs/guide site framework.

entries.name: VitePress
entries.use_for: Vite and Vue powered static site generator for documentation.
entries.why: Very fast builds and a clean default theme; used by Vue, Vite and many libraries.
entries.summary: VitePress is a Vue-powered static site generator built on top of Vite and a spiritual successor to VuePress. It is commonly used to build documentation sites.
entries.best_for: Fast documentation or content sites for teams comfortable with Vue and Vite.
entries.not_for: Vue/Vite stack; teams standardized on React or another framework may prefer alternatives. Not an API reference renderer.
